4.0.name: entity_type
4.0.description: Type(s) of entities in the claim (taxonomy-aware). Extract up to 3 types if multiple entity categories present. Values: Gene, Protein, Drug, Disease, Pathway, Cell, Tissue, Receptor, Enzyme, Virus, Bacteria, Hormone, Metabolite, RNA, DNA, Process. Example: 'Gene, Protein' for 'p53 protein encoded by TP53 gene'

6.0.name: causal_agent
6.0.description: Entity/entities PERFORMING the action (the cause/intervention). Extract up to 3 key entities. Examples: 'Statins', 'MDA5', 'SIRT1, FOXO3, ROS'

10.0.name: causal_target
10.0.description: Entity/entities BEING AFFECTED by the action (the target/patient). Extract up to 3 key targets. Examples: 'cholesterol', 'RNA_virus', 'stem_cells, nanotechnology'

12.0.name: causal_verb
12.0.description: Causal verbs describing the relationship. Extract BOTH hypothesis AND findings if present. Values: increases, decreases, causes, prevents, binds, activates, inhibits, regulates, associated_with, not_associated_with. Example: 'decreases_risk_of, not_associated_with' (hypothesis + null finding)

18.0.name: effect_outcome
18.0.description: The downstream effect or outcome of the causal relationship. Be specific about what happens as a result. Examples: 'reduced_disease_risk', 'immune_response_activation', 'cell_death'

19.0.name: finding_type
19.0.description: Type of finding in the document (intrinsic to document, not query-dependent). positive_finding = confirms hypothesis, negative_finding = contradicts hypothesis, null_finding = no significant effect found

24.0.name: causal_position
24.0.description: Position in the causal chain (A→B→C). Enables chain detection: intervention→mechanism→outcome

30.0.name: sample_size
30.0.description: Number of subjects/samples (proxy for confidence level)

50.0.name: evidence_type
50.0.description: Type of evidence supporting the claim

70.0.name: key_claim
70.0.description: Full semantic summary of the main claim (5-15 words)
